_note: REAL measured numbers from jev_scoring.py on an Apple M1 8GB laptop (MPS, fp32). Reproduce with: python3 jev_scoring.py [--model_id ...]. Nothing here is simulated. Accuracy is low because 135M models are tiny; that is the honest point (mechanism != accuracy).
machine: Apple M1, 8GB unified memory, MPS backend, torch 2.14, transformers 5.17

head_to_head_routing.generation_raw_text: {\n  "choice": "billing", ... (correct choice, but slow and needs parsing)

honest_findings: The scoring mechanism (read option-token logits from the KEPT lm_head, restricted softmax, one forward pass) is real and produces a genuine distribution from the pretrained model -- NOT the uniform 1/K noise that the earlier untrained bolt-on heads produced.
Scoring is ~20-26x faster than generation even on a 135M model on a laptop, with 0 output tokens; the gap widens on bigger models and longer generations, consistent with TypeSafe's 40-200x claim.

Accuracy is a SEPARATE axis from the mechanism. 135M models (base or instruct) are too small to route this ticket correctly -- both mis-route to 'frontend' with ~0.11 confidence (near chance). JEV-CPU reports 0.44 balanced accuracy at 0.6B, rising to 0.69 at 2B and 0.81 at 4B.

Nuance: on the instruct model, single-token letter-scoring mis-routed while free generation got 'billing' right. Tiny models' first-token distribution at the label position is not always aligned; capable models + calibration (RLCD) are what make scoring both fast AND accurate.
The autoregressive baseline on the base model emitted an INVALID choice ('1') and rambled -- concrete evidence that generation is both slower and structurally fragile.
